title: Ishango Bone
summary: A 10 cm bone topped with a quartz fragment, found in 1950 by geologist Jean de Heinzelin on the Congolese bank of Lake Edward near Ishango, now in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Its notches appear in groups, and the museum puts its age at nearly 20,000 years; another source gives a wider range.

uncertainty.note: Museum says nearly 20,000 years old; UNESCO portal gives a re-evaluated range of c. 25,000 BP to 16,000 BP. Year is a rounded stand-in for the about-20,000-years figure.

when.display: c. 20,000 years ago (range c. 25,000–16,000 BP); found 1950

where.modern_name: Ishango, Virunga National Park, Democratic Republic of the Congo
where.historical_name: Ishango, Lake Edward shore (prehistoric site; excavated 1950 in the Belgian Congo)

importance.justification: Frequently cited early engraved object, debated as evidence of prehistoric counting.
